agent.label: Agent
agent.description:
An agent that works with Atlas. The id is short and lower case, made from the
name, e.g. coordinator.

cannot_run.description: Where and since when it cannot run, and why (3 crashes in 10 minutes); Runtime writes and clears it (IS-Atlas-18)

agent_request.label: Agent request
agent_request.description:
What Melle asked the agent on a page of the TUI (`:`), and what became of
it: the plan's summary and its outcome. Its steps hang under it. The cause
of every change the agent made (SC-Atlas-04, UC-Atlas-19).

before.description: What became of the previous plan, after a refusal

page.description: The page it was asked on

summary.description: What the agent said about its plan

agent_step.label: Agent step
agent_step.description:
One step of a request's plan: the form it filled, with what values, and
what became of it, with the key of the item it made, changed or deleted.

detail.description: The id it stored, or why it was refused

made.description: The key of the item it made, changed or deleted

title.description: The title of the form it filled

values.description: The values it gave, as JSON

was.description: For a change: the values it replaced, as JSON

assignment.label: Assignment
assignment.description:
What belongs to being assigned, for one fact: who it is assigned to and what
they are expected to do. Made and deleted with the fact; its id is AS- and the
fact's, e.g. AS-UC-Atlas-01.

deadline.description: When it should be done by; optional, it only marks it late (IS-Atlas-14)

expected.description: What its owner is expected to do next; Flow writes it (IS-Atlas-53)

flow_state.description: The state of its flow it is in; Flow writes it (IS-Atlas-54)

handover.description: A deferred automatic handover; Flow keeps it until the running owner ends its turn

of.description: The key of the fact it belongs to

decision.label: Decision
decision.description:
One decision record in the append-only ledger: the rule, why, and what follows
from it. An accepted decision is never edited; a newer decision supersedes it. The id
is D- and a number, e.g. D-0024.

decided_at.description: When it was accepted or rejected

decision.description: The rule, in one or two sentences

enforced_by.description: The test, check or gate that enforces it; required for a principle

gate_result.description: Flow: gate activity result; the durable run holds its trusted source

no_work.description: True when carrying it out needs no work; it then waits for none

title.description: The decision in a few words

unverified.description: An agent decided after the person answer limit; cleared by review

verdict.description: Flow: the verdict of whoever may decide it (none, accept, reject)

flow_input.label: Flow input
flow_input.description: Typed trusted choice operation, prepared before its subject write.

flow_run.label: Flow run
flow_run.description: Durable generated state machine cursor, written only by its runner.

gate_verdict.label: Gate verdict

activity_digest.description: Frozen activity payload digest; reuse with another payload is refused

activity_id.description: Durable caller activity identity, when asked by Flow

advisor.description: Who advised a smart gate, e.g. jev

allowed_outcomes.description: The outcomes it could choose, separated by commas

cost.description: What the evaluation cost, e.g. 0.012 USD

defect_after.description: Later, a problem found afterwards, and where

duration_ms.description: How long the evaluation took, in milliseconds

effort.description: Later, the time and human effort spent after it

evidence.description: References to the evidence it decided on, one per line

evidence_digest.description: The content digest of the immutable evidence snapshot, e.g. sha256:...

fingerprint.description: The exact version of the subject it decided on

gate_version.description: The version of the gate's definition that decided

model.description: The model, prompt and evaluator settings the advice came from

overrule_reason.description: Later, why a person overruled it

rationale.description: Why the advice is what it is

rework_after.description: Later, the rework needed after all, and what showed it

scores.description: The advice per outcome, as text, e.g. pass 0.7, changes_required 0.3

subject.description: What it decided on, the key or reference of the fact or change

unsettled.description: Uncertain or error, when the gate could not decide on its own

verdict.description: The outcome the gate chose; one of allowed_outcomes

interaction.label: Interaction
interaction.description: Immutable durable interaction; only the Facts guidance operation writes this record.

interaction_receipt.label: Interaction receipt
interaction_receipt.description: Immutable durable receipt; only the Facts guidance operation writes this record.

issue.label: Issue
issue.description:
Small, independently testable work, normally one pull request (Flux's
meaning). The id is its Atlas code, e.g. IS-Atlas-01.

effect_result.description: Flow: how publishing the pull request ended (none, done, refused)

flux_id.description: Flux (Basecamp) id, set by a later Flux sync

flux_ref.description: Flux's own issue code (ref), e.g. NEXT-240, set by a later Flux sync

gate_result.description: Flow: the last gate verdict, or a maintainer's choice (none, review, rework, ready, person, close)

pass_result.description: Flow: how the last pass ended (none, delivered, failed)

pr_outcome.description: Flow: where its pull request is (none, open, changes_requested, integrated, closed)

person.label: Person
person.description:
Someone who works with Atlas. The id is short and lower case, made from
the name, e.g. melle.

pr_review.label: PR review
pr_review.description:
The review of one pull request by a person, created by the pull request's
flow. Its outcome is reported back to the pull request.

superseded.description: True when a newer revision of the pull request replaced this review

verdict.description: The reviewer's verdict: approved or changes_requested

pr_test.label: PR test
pr_test.description:
The test of one pull request by a person, created by the pull request's
flow. Its outcome is reported back to the pull request.

superseded.description: True when a newer revision of the pull request replaced this test

verdict.description: The tester's verdict: passed or failed

pull_request.label: Pull request
pull_request.description:
A GitHub pull request for an issue. Linked by URL; a GitHub connector
fills title and state later. The id is derived from the URL,
PR-<owner>-<repo>-<number>, so linking the same URL twice is one record.

integration.description: Flow: how integrating it ended, or a maintainer's retry (none, done, refused, retry)

review_outcome.description: Flow: how its review ended (none, approved, changes_requested)

test_outcome.description: Flow: how its test ended (none, passed, failed)

update.description: Flow: updated when a new revision arrives after changes were requested (none, updated)

scene.label: Scene
scene.description:
An actor-centred view of the system, with one angle and one zoom level
(Flux's meaning). The id is its code, e.g. SC-Atlas-01.

children.description: Flow: how many use cases are in it

flux_id.description: Flux (Basecamp) id, set by a later Flux sync

open_children.description: Flow: how many of them are not finished

pass_result.description: Flow: how the last pass ended (none, delivered, failed)

verdict.description: Flow: the acceptor's verdict (none, accept, reject)

turn.label: Turn
turn.description:
One stretch in which an agent acts on one item: started by Runtime for the item's
owner, kept while the agent shows activity (its lease), ended when the agent ends
it, goes silent, crashes, runs too long, or no longer owns the item.

activity.description: The agent's last activity Runtime saw

attempt.description: Runtime execution fence; a new attempt never inherits old guidance.

lease_until.description: Until when the turn holds its lease: the agent's last activity plus the silence limit

machine.description: The machine whose Runtime runs it

outcome.description: The agent's fact about what it did; Runtime reads it and ends the turn

use_case.label: Use case
use_case.description:
The technical contract for part of a scene (Flux's meaning). The id is
its code, e.g. UC-Atlas-01.

children.description: Flow: how many issues are in it

design.description: The Design part: how it is built, written by the Architect

design_status.description: Where the Design part is; empty for a use case without a design phase

flux_id.description: Flux (Basecamp) id, set by a later Flux sync

gate_result.description: Flow: the last design gate verdict, or a maintainer's choice (none, review, rework, ready, person, close)

open_children.description: Flow: how many of them are not finished

pass_result.description: Flow: how the last pass ended (none, delivered, failed)

verdict.description: Flow: the acceptor's verdict (none, accept, reject)

worker_execution.label: Worker execution
worker_execution.description: Immutable durable execution; only the Facts guidance operation writes this record.

about.label: about
about.description: The fact a gate verdict decided on; any kind the composition has.

accepted_by.label: accepted by
accepted_by.description: Who accepted a scene or use case, after testing it; at most one.

assigned_to.label: assigned to
assigned_to.description: Who is next in line to do something with it; one, a person or an agent.

assignment.label: assignment
assignment.description: What belongs to being assigned, for one fact; made and deleted with it.

based_on.label: based on
based_on.description: The decisions this work carries out; optional, most work has none.

decided_by.label: decided by
decided_by.description: Who accepted or rejected the decision; one, a person or an agent.

delegated_by.label: delegated by
delegated_by.description: The person whose delegated authority an agent decided under; at most one.

done_in.label: also done in
done_in.description: A merged pull request of another issue that also did this one.

follows.label: follows
follows.description: The previous verdict on the same subject; verdicts so form an episode.

follows_from.label: follows from
follows_from.description: The higher-level decisions this one elaborates.

in_issue.label: in issue
in_issue.description: A pull request belongs to at most one issue; an issue has zero or more pull requests.

in_request.label: in request
in_request.description: A step belongs to the request whose plan it was part of.

in_scene.label: in scene
in_scene.description: A use case belongs to at most one scene (Flux); a scene has zero or more use cases.

in_use_case.label: in use case
in_use_case.description: An issue belongs to at most one use case (Flux); a use case has zero or more issues.

overruled_by.label: overruled by
overruled_by.description: Later, the person who overruled the verdict; at most one.

review_of.label: review of
review_of.description: A review belongs to one pull request; a pull request has its reviews.

reviewed_by.label: confirmed by
reviewed_by.description: The person who confirms an unverified verdict; set once to themselves.

supersedes.label: supersedes
supersedes.description: The accepted decisions this one replaces; they become superseded when it is accepted.

test_of.label: test of
test_of.description: A test belongs to one pull request; a pull request has its tests.

turn_by.label: by
turn_by.description: The agent that acts in the turn.

turn_on.label: on
turn_on.description: The item the turn acts on.
